This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner seeking following reliefs:-
"(i) Issue writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding to respondents, specially respondent nos. 5, 6 and 7 of National Highway Authority of India to either re-construct brutally damaged Temple of Vishwaveshwar Nath Mahadev Ji Virajman, petitioner no. 1 including demolished integral part of temple viz. is "Shelter House", "Satsang Bhawan", "Gaushala", water-well" and "room of worship men" in total area of about 5000 sq. fts. either on land of petitioner no. 1 provided by her with her sweet will.

sentences.text: (iii) Issue writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding to respondents no. 2 and 4 to provide land bearing Gata No. 5322 in same village-Ittaura Bujurg, Tehsil Uncchahar, District Raibariely v.i.z. near to present demolished site as well as from village of petitioner no. 2, in case the respondents- NHAI asking for land for reconstruction of damaged Temple of Vishwaveshwar Nath Mahadev Ji Virajman, petitioner no. 1 including demolished integral part of temple viz. is "Shelter House", "Satsang Bhawan", "Gaushala", water-well" and "room of worship men" presently existing in total area of about 5000 sq. fts.

(iv) Issue writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding to respondents- NHAI also construct demolished integral and adjacent part of"Shelter House", "Satsang Bhawan", "Gaushala", water-well" and "room of worship men"
presently existing in total area of about 5000 sq. fts. adjacent to, if any, proposed site of Temple of Vishwaveshwar Nath Mahadev Ji Virajman, petitioner no. 1."
There are two petitioners, petitioner no. 1 is Shri Vishwaveshwar Nath Mahadev Ji Virajman and petitioner no. 2 is Smt. Urmila Pandey, who claims to be the Caretaker/Worshipper at the temple.
Contention of petitioner's counsel is that the temple was built by her husband on the land which neither belonged to her husband nor her.
Land bears Gata No. 5322 and is situated at village Ittaura Bujurg, Tehsil Uncchahar, District Rae Bareli.
This land is recorded in the revenue records as forest land, as submitted by petitioner's counsel.
Now the land has been acquired by NHAI for being used for construction of National Highway.
As the land does not belong to the petitioner, therefore, she cannot claim compensation.

If she is claiming any other benefit such as shifting of the temple or the idols installed therein, then she can approach the concerned opposite parties in this regard, who may look into the matter but beyond this, we cannot pass any order in her favour.

sentences.text: At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioner says that the opposite parties may build a temple at the petitioner's land in lieu of the temple which they seek to demolish.
We fail to understand as to how we can consider this prayer under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
The petitioners may approach the opposite parties with this requesting it is otherwise permissible.
Writ petition is disposed of.
